claim: Submit rate and test-verified resolve rate diverge: GPT-5 submits 100% and resolves 44%; Llama 4 99% vs 18%; Gemini submits 70% but resolves 50%, ranking differently from submit rate.
stance_target: F: completion/indicator metrics mismeasure construct; instrument-validity framing for coding agents
scope_conditions: 50 SWE-bench Verified tasks, 5 runs each, 4 models, mini-SWE-agent, Table 1
quoted_support: By submit rate, meaning whether the agent produces a patch, GPT-5 looks perfect: 100% across 250 runs on SWE-bench. By resolve rate, whether the patch passes the project's tests, it drops to 44%.

breadth.confidence_families: none; indicators are submit rate, step CV, patch similarity, loop detector (Sec 2, 5)
breadth.model_families_and_sizes: Claude 4.5 Sonnet, GPT-5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Llama 4 Maverick via hosted APIs, sizes not stated (Sec 4)
breadth.elicitation_formats: not present (searched: verbalized confidence); pre-edit interpretation and test-anchored guards (Sec 4)
breadth.label_independence: execution criterion independent of agent self-report
breadth.calibration_metrics: resolve rate, SSFR, step CV, bootstrap leaderboards; no ECE/AUROC (Sec 5)

claim: The paper explicitly frames agent evaluation as construct measurement (construct, indicator, criterion; reliability x validity grid), citing Messick 1989 and Jacobs and Wallach 2021; it is about agent success metrics, not confidence calibration.
stance_target: F: measurement/metrology framing exists in coding-agent evaluation but not applied to confidence estimators
quoted_support: We borrow the language of measurement science and psychometrics on purpose (Messick, 1989; Jacobs and Wallach, 2021).
numbers: silent semantic failure rate 80% Llama 4, 68% GPT-5, 40% Claude, 16% Gemini

claim: Cheap process features (3-gram command loops, trajectory length r = -0.26) partially recover the missing validity signal without tests; two pre-edit guard prompts do not change resolve rate (GPT-5 44.4% to 46.0% and 44.0%).
stance_target: L3: test-free signals for routing; no verbal confidence studied
quoted_support: Neither guard moves overall resolve rate: the interpretation guard leaves Claude at 65.2% to 64.8% and GPT-5 at 44.4% to 46.0%.
